title: Read what the evaluator really runs
statement: Learn and report what a judge or gate actually does from its code and saved verdicts, tested on a few items, not from documentation or a published description.
example: One report presented a borrowed benchmark's error-correction task score as curriculum alignment, at 10.00 out of 10.
detail: A reading QC rubric's published page asks feedback on a wrong option to give a path to the right answer 'without giving it away directly' (`icloud-work/incept/incept-uae-api-website/bench.inceptapi.com/content/english/pages/us-reading-comprehension.md`), but the prompt file the pipeline names as 'All quality control prompts' passes feedback that states the correct answer outright (`icloud-work/incept/incept-multilingual-generation/src/external_submodules/reading-question-qc/qc_pipeline/config/prompts.json`). Separately, a benchmark report gives 'Educational Curriculum Alignment (EC)' as 10.00/10.0 on 873 items (`icloud-work/incept/incept-multilingual-generation/src/evaluator/reports/incept_benchmark_report.md`). In the borrowed benchmark EC is Error Correction (`icloud-work/incept/incept-multilingual-generation/src/evaluator/EduBench/README.md`), and the evaluator's notes say its task mode tests how well a model can respond to the question (`icloud-work/incept/incept-multilingual-generation/src/evaluator/Readme.md`). Read a judge's criteria, weights and caps in its own source, and test them on a few items. A guess from the failures misled one generator: the judge's failure comments asked for a spread of difficulty, but adding a progression raised difficulty faults from 50% to 86% of that item type's failures, because the judge checks each question against the requested level (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/benchmark_results/unit_1/diagnosis.md`, line 17; `icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/data/model_findings.md`, lines 1125 and 1176). A read of the judge's code found two critical metrics at double weight and a veto cap of 0.84 (`icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/full-copy/aptraining-root/achieved.md`, line 133).
against: The project's framework document makes the same relabelling openly, describing the Error Correction row as 'Tests curriculum alignment and educational appropriateness. Does content match grade-level standards?' (`icloud-work/incept/incept-uae-api-website/inceptapi.com/INCEPT_Benchmarking_Framework.html`, lines 261-263). The judge flips verdicts on identical item sets often ("DBQ flips 30%, MCQ_SET 50%", `icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/CLAUDE.md`, line 101), so part of the rise from 50% to 86% may be noise. The double weight and the 0.84 cap are reported from a read of the judge's code, not quoted from it.

1. **`edubench_tasks`** (AI Model Response Testing): Tests how well an AI model (EDU-Qwen2.5-7B) can respond to your question across 6 task types (QA, EC, IP, AG, QG, TMG). This validates that your question is clear enough for AI to understand.
**Why MCQ_SET regressed (-10.8pp):** Generator prompt mandated uniform difficulty → evaluator's difficulty_distribution hard-fails.
Gate 13 running immediately after fixes. Same model (sft-v3-14b), same N=100, prompt-only changes.
The progressive difficulty change caused `difficulty_distribution` to jump from **50% → 86%** of MCQ_SET failures.
The evaluator does NOT want Q1<Q2<Q3 difficulty — it wants all 3 at the SAME stated difficulty level.
The difficulty distribution is narrow; there are no 'Easy' questions present, and over 60% of the quiz sits at the Medium level. This lacks the progression needed for effective differentiation.
**InceptBench rubric: 5 dimensions, weighted; pass threshold 0.85 (corrected from 0.75 in newer harness).**
**InceptBench rubric — actual 11 metrics for `question` content type** (correction to the earlier 5-dim claim)
Identified BAML/Gemini grader, CRITICAL_VETO_CAP=0.84, critical metrics (factual_accuracy + educational_accuracy 2× weight).
**Reference for every agent: schema before training rows; rubric before scoring expectations; curriculum before factual claims.**
